flags.description: Compares total row counts between model and reference outputs.
flags.sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Compares distinct customer_id counts between model and reference.
flags.sql: SELECT 'distinct_customers' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM model_output)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT customer_id) FROM reference_output)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Lists customer_ids present in only one of the two tables with a presence flag for each side.
flags.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM model_output), r AS (SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM reference_output) SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, CASE WHEN m.customer_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS model_value, CASE WHEN r.customer_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE m.customer_id IS NULL OR r.customer_id IS NULL

flags.description: Grand total of lifetime_revenue across all customers.
flags.sql: SELECT 'total_lifetime_revenue' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Grand total of lifetime_orders across all customers.
flags.sql: SELECT 'total_lifetime_orders' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_orders) FROM model_output)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_orders) FROM reference_output)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Overall average order value computed as total revenue divided by total orders, to catch fan-out or division distortions.
flags.sql: SELECT 'weighted_avg_order_value' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue)/SUM(lifetime_orders) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue)/SUM(lifetime_orders) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Unweighted mean of avg_order_supply_cost across customers, ignoring nulls.
flags.sql: SELECT 'mean_avg_order_supply_cost' AS slice, (SELECT AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Order-weighted average of avg_order_supply_cost, to detect distortion from null handling on no-item orders.
flags.sql: SELECT 'weighted_avg_order_supply_cost' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(avg_order_supply_cost*lifetime_orders)/SUM(CASE WHEN avg_order_supply_cost IS NOT NULL THEN lifetime_orders ELSE 0 END) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(avg_order_supply_cost*lifetime_orders)/SUM(CASE WHEN avg_order_supply_cost IS NOT NULL THEN lifetime_orders ELSE 0 END) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Count of customers with a null avg_order_supply_cost (should only occur when all qualifying orders lack item records).
flags.sql: SELECT 'null_avg_order_supply_cost_count' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE avg_order_supply_cost IS NULL)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE avg_order_supply_cost IS NULL)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Count of customers with avg_order_supply_cost exactly zero, to catch no-item orders incorrectly treated as zero cost instead of excluded.
flags.sql: SELECT 'zero_avg_order_supply_cost_count' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE avg_order_supply_cost = 0)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE avg_order_supply_cost = 0)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Count of customers with zero lifetime_orders, which should never occur given the qualifying-order join.
flags.sql: SELECT 'zero_order_customers' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 0)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 0)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Per-customer comparison of lifetime_revenue.
flags.sql: SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.lifetime_revenue AS model_value, r.lifetime_revenue AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

flags.description: Per-customer comparison of lifetime_orders.
flags.sql: SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.lifetime_orders AS model_value, r.lifetime_orders AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

flags.description: Per-customer comparison of avg_order_value.
flags.sql: SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.avg_order_value AS model_value, r.avg_order_value AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

flags.description: Per-customer comparison of avg_order_supply_cost.
flags.sql: SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.avg_order_supply_cost AS model_value, r.avg_order_supply_cost AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

flags.description: Per-customer comparison of first_order_date expressed as days since epoch.
flags.sql: SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', m.first_order_date) AS model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', r.first_order_date) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

flags.description: Per-customer comparison of last_order_date expressed as days since epoch.
flags.sql: SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', m.last_order_date) AS model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', r.last_order_date) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

flags.description: Count of matching customer_ids where customer_name differs between model and reference; expected to be zero.
flags.sql: SELECT 'customer_name_mismatch_count' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output m JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE m.customer_name IS DISTINCT FROM r.customer_name)::DOUBLE AS model_value, 0::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Lifetime revenue summed by the year of first_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) AS VARCHAR) AS slice, SUM(m.lifetime_revenue) AS model_value, SUM(r.lifetime_revenue) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Lifetime revenue summed by the year-month of first_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT STRFTIME(COALESCE(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date), '%Y-%m') AS slice, SUM(m.lifetime_revenue) AS model_value, SUM(r.lifetime_revenue) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Lifetime revenue summed by the year of last_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(m.last_order_date, r.last_order_date)) AS VARCHAR) AS slice, SUM(m.lifetime_revenue) AS model_value, SUM(r.lifetime_revenue) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Lifetime revenue summed by the year-month of last_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT STRFTIME(COALESCE(m.last_order_date, r.last_order_date), '%Y-%m') AS slice, SUM(m.lifetime_revenue) AS model_value, SUM(r.lifetime_revenue) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Count of customers by the week (Monday-start) of first_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT STRFTIME(DATE_TRUNC('week', COALESCE(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)), '%Y-%m-%d') AS slice, COUNT(m.customer_id) AS model_value, COUNT(r.customer_id) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Count of customers by the exact day of first_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT STRFTIME(COALESCE(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date), '%Y-%m-%d') AS slice, COUNT(m.customer_id) AS model_value, COUNT(r.customer_id) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Lifetime_orders summed by the year of first_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) AS VARCHAR) AS slice, SUM(m.lifetime_orders) AS model_value, SUM(r.lifetime_orders) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Lifetime_orders summed by the year of last_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(m.last_order_date, r.last_order_date)) AS VARCHAR) AS slice, SUM(m.lifetime_orders) AS model_value, SUM(r.lifetime_orders) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Earliest first_order_date overall, expressed as days since epoch, to check boundary alignment.
flags.sql: SELECT 'min_first_order_date' AS slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (SELECT MIN(first_order_date) FROM model_output)) AS model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (SELECT MIN(first_order_date) FROM reference_output)) AS reference_value

flags.description: Latest last_order_date overall, expressed as days since epoch, to check boundary alignment.
flags.sql: SELECT 'max_last_order_date' AS slice, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (SELECT MAX(last_order_date) FROM model_output)) AS model_value, date_diff('day', DATE '1970-01-01', (SELECT MAX(last_order_date) FROM reference_output)) AS reference_value

flags.description: Total revenue among customers with exactly one lifetime order.
flags.sql: SELECT 'single_order_customers_revenue' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM model_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 1) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM reference_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 1) AS reference_value

flags.description: Count of single-order customers where avg_order_value does not equal lifetime_revenue; expected zero mismatches.
flags.sql: SELECT 'single_order_avg_value_mismatch_count' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 1 AND ABS(avg_order_value - lifetime_revenue) > 0.01)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 1 AND ABS(avg_order_value - lifetime_revenue) > 0.01)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Lifetime_revenue comparison for the top 20 customers ranked by reference revenue.
flags.sql: WITH top AS (SELECT customer_id FROM reference_output ORDER BY lifetime_revenue DESC LIMIT 20) SELECT t.customer_id AS slice, m.lifetime_revenue AS model_value, r.lifetime_revenue AS reference_value FROM top t LEFT JOIN model_output m ON m.customer_id = t.customer_id LEFT JOIN reference_output r ON r.customer_id = t.customer_id

flags.description: Lifetime revenue summed by year-quarter of first_order_date.
flags.sql: SELECT CONCAT(CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM COALESCE(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) AS VARCHAR), '-Q', CAST(EXTRACT(QUARTER FROM COALESCE(m.first_order_date, r.first_order_date)) AS VARCHAR)) AS slice, SUM(m.lifetime_revenue) AS model_value, SUM(r.lifetime_revenue) AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Count of customers with a non-null avg_order_supply_cost, i.e. at least one qualifying order with item records.
flags.sql: SELECT 'customers_with_supply_cost_data' AS slice, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM model_output WHERE avg_order_supply_cost IS NOT NULL)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM reference_output WHERE avg_order_supply_cost IS NOT NULL)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

flags.description: Unweighted mean of per-customer avg_order_value across all customers.
flags.sql: SELECT 'simple_mean_avg_order_value' AS slice, (SELECT AVG(avg_order_value) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT AVG(avg_order_value) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Maximum lifetime_orders value across all customers, to check for outlier/fan-out distortions.
flags.sql: SELECT 'max_lifetime_orders' AS slice, (SELECT MAX(lifetime_orders) FROM model_output)::DOUBLE AS model_value, (SELECT MAX(lifetime_orders) FROM reference_output)::DOUBLE AS reference_value

ai.prompt:
A dbt model has been changed and must be reconciled against an independent reference dashboard before it ships.

## Model: customer_lifetime_value

### Business definition (from the model's YAML)
Lifetime value per customer. One row per real customer with at least one qualifying order (internal "QA Test Account" customers and refunded orders are excluded). lifetime_revenue is the sum of qualifying order totals including tax. avg_order_value is lifetime_revenue / lifetime_orders. avg_order_supply_cost is the mean supply cost over qualifying orders that have item records; orders with no item records are excluded from the average rather than counted as zero.

### Model SQL (dbt/Jinja, DuckDB dialect)
```sql
with

orders as (

    select * from {{ ref('orders') }}

),

customers as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_customers') }}

),

refunds as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_refunds') }}

),

qualifying_orders as (

    select
        orders.*,
        customers.customer_name

    from orders

    inner join customers
        on orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id

    left join refunds
        on orders.order_id = refunds.order_id

    where refunds.order_id is null

)

select
    qualifying_orders.customer_id,
    qualifying_orders.customer_name,
    cast(min(qualifying_orders.ordered_at_ts) as date) as first_order_date,
    cast(max(qualifying_orders.ordered_at_ts) as date) as last_order_date,
    cast(count(qualifying_orders.order_id) as bigint) as lifetime_orders,
    cast(sum(qualifying_orders.order_total) as decimal(18, 2)) as lifetime_revenue,
    cast(sum(qualifying_orders.order_total) as double)
        / count(qualifying_orders.order_id) as avg_order_value,
    cast(avg(qualifying_orders.order_cost) as double) as avg_order_supply_cost

from qualifying_orders

group by 1, 2
```

## Tables available to your queries
Your queries run in a sandbox that contains exactly two tables and nothing else:

`model_output`: the model's output.
  - customer_id: VARCHAR
  - customer_name: VARCHAR
  - first_order_date: DATE
  - last_order_date: DATE
  - lifetime_orders: BIGINT
  - lifetime_revenue: DECIMAL(18,2)
  - avg_order_value: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_supply_cost: DOUBLE

`reference_output`: the trusted reference dashboard, computed independently from raw data at the same grain.
  - customer_id: VARCHAR
  - customer_name: VARCHAR
  - first_order_date: DATE
  - last_order_date: DATE
  - lifetime_orders: BIGINT
  - lifetime_revenue: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_value: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_supply_cost: DOUBLE

Grain (one row per): customer_id

## Task
Write up to 40 reconciliation queries comparing `model_output` to `reference_output`. Choose slices that would expose wrong numbers that still pass schema checks and data tests, for example: grand totals of each measure; totals by each dimension and dimension member; each available time grain (day, week, month, as applicable); edge periods (first/last periods, period boundaries); row counts and key coverage (keys present in one table but not the other); and averages/ratios where nulls or join fan-out could distort them.

Each query MUST return exactly these columns:
- `slice` (varchar): a human-readable label for the row, e.g. 'total', '2025-03 | Brooklyn'
- `model_value` (numeric): the value computed from model_output
- `reference_value` (numeric): the same value computed from reference_output

A query may return one row (a total) or many rows (one per slice). Use a full outer join on the slice keys so that slices missing on either side appear, with NULL on the missing side. Do not compute differences yourself; the harness compares model_value to reference_value. Return at most 5000 rows per query.
